framework.summary: Large frontier developers must write, follow and publish a frontier AI framework, and review it at least once a year.
framework.quote: A large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a frontier AI framework

transparency_report.summary: Every frontier developer must publish a transparency report when it deploys a new or substantially modified frontier model.
transparency_report.quote: a frontier developer shall clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a transparency report

incident_reporting.summary: Critical safety incidents must be reported to the state office within 72 hours of a determination or of learning enough facts to believe one occurred.
incident_reporting.quote: shall report any critical safety incident pertaining to one or more of its frontier models to the office within seventy-two hours

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: An incident posing an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury must be disclosed to an appropriate authority within 24 hours.
imminent_risk_reporting.quote: poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury, the frontier developer shall disclose that incident within twenty-four hours

third_party_audit.summary: The framework must describe how the developer uses third parties to assess catastrophic risk; no independent audit is required.
third_party_audit.quote: using third parties to assess the potential for catastrophic risks and the effectiveness of mitigations of catastrophic risks

whistleblower.summary: The text has no whistleblower provision.

registration.summary: A large frontier developer may not develop, deploy or operate a frontier model in New York without a current disclosure statement filed with the state office, renewed every two years.
registration.quote: no large frontier developer may develop, deploy, or operate a frontier model, in whole or in part in New York state, without having a current disclosure statement filed with the office

shutdown.summary: The text requires no shutdown or kill-switch capability.

compute_threshold.summary: A frontier model is one trained with more than 10^26 operations, counting fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.
compute_threshold.quote: a foundation model that was trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 10

revenue_threshold.summary: A large frontier developer has annual gross revenues above $500,000,000, with its affiliates, in the preceding calendar year.
revenue_threshold.quote: annual gross revenues in excess of five hundred million dollars in the preceding calendar year

harm_threshold.summary: Catastrophic risk means death or serious injury to more than 50 people, or more than $1,000,000,000 in property damage, from a single incident.
harm_threshold.quote: more than fifty people or more than one billion dollars in damage to, or loss of, property arising from a single incident

penalties.summary: Attorney General may sue large frontier developers for up to $1,000,000 for a first violation and $3,000,000 per later one; the state office may also fine $1,000 a day for not filing the disclosure statement.
penalties.quote: in an amount not to exceed one million dollars for a first violation and in an amount not to exceed three million dollars per subsequent violation

effective_date.summary: Sec. 3 sets the 2025 Act's effective date to January 1, 2027; under Sec. 5 this bill takes effect immediately, but its new article takes effect when that 2025 Act does.
